title: RocketKV: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Two-Stage KV Cache Compression
one_line_claim: Two-stage KV cache compression combining permanent token eviction and hybrid sparse attention achieves up to 400x compression and 3.7x speedup with negligible accuracy loss.
method_summary: RocketKV applies SnapKV for coarse-grain permanent KV token eviction on input sequences, then uses hybrid sparse attention (HSA) with top-k selection and two-dimensional dimensionality reductions to perform fine-grain dynamic token selection during decoding. A multi-turn variant preserves all KV tokens across turns while filtering within turns.

key_findings.finding: Existing KV token dropping methods fail to match oracle top-k attention accuracy; accuracy drops significantly below 1024 token budget.
key_findings.quote: We observe that the accuracy of all four methods drops significantly as the token budget becomes lower than 1024

key_findings.finding: RocketKV achieves compression ratio up to 400x with end-to-end speedup 3.7x and peak memory reduction 32.6%.
key_findings.quote: compression ratio of up to 400x, end-to-end speedup of up to 3.7x as well as peak memory reduction of up to 32.6% in the decode phase on an NVIDIA A100 GPU

key_findings.finding: Maintains comparable accuracy to full KV across LongBench, RULER, and Needle-in-a-Haystack while outperforming other compression methods.
key_findings.quote: RocketKV consistently demonstrates comparable accuracy with full KV attention while significantly lowering memory bandwidth and capacity usage with a compression ratio of up to 400x

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV cache compression as a source of inference degradation and operate during the decode phase.
differs_on: RocketKV proposes a new compression method; HERALD treats any compressor as a black box and predicts failure modes from logit signals.
RocketKV maintains accuracy under compression through token selection heuristics; HERALD detects when compression has caused catastrophic failures.
RocketKV measures end-to-end speedup; HERALD measures early-warning prediction accuracy for collapse scenarios.
